scope: security-only (user-requested focused re-run #3, not the full 12-pillar audit)

pillars.title: Security

criteria.statement: Least-privilege IAM (no wildcard * actions/resources without justification)
criteria.notes: New cloudtrail_to_cw role is well-scoped; Bedrock InvokeModel Resource remains wildcarded (SEC-F4), unchanged.

criteria.statement: No long-lived credentials/secrets in code or state.
Encryption at rest on all data stores.
criteria.notes: New CloudTrail S3 bucket also SSE-KMS encrypted (AWS-managed key).

criteria.statement: No public exposure of data stores/admin surfaces unless justified.
criteria.notes: New CloudTrail bucket also fully public-access-blocked.

criteria.statement: KMS CMK usage & key rotation where appropriate.
criteria.notes: New CloudTrail resources consistently use AWS-managed keys, not a new gap (SEC-F2).

criteria.statement: Detective controls (CloudTrail, Config, GuardDuty, Security Hub) enabled.
criteria.notes: CloudTrail + GuardDuty now correctly enabled — substantial improvement. Held at Partial: neither the new alarms nor GuardDuty findings have a default notification path (alarm_actions defaults to []), and Config/Security Hub remain entirely absent.

criteria.statement: Secrets not logged; PII handling & redaction.

criteria.notes: No CI/CD pipeline exists; nothing to assess.
Now includes a distinct cloudtrail_to_cw role in addition to webhook/worker/runtime_execution.

strengths.text: A genuine, correctly-built account-wide detective baseline now exists: multi-region CloudTrail with global service events and log file validation, a least-privilege log-delivery IAM role, and a GuardDuty detector.
The CloudTrail S3 bucket policy correctly implements AWS's documented required statements; bucket is fully public-access-blocked and encrypted.
Two purpose-built metric filter + alarm pairs target the most security-relevant event classes (IAM changes, Secrets Manager read volume) with sensibly differentiated thresholds.
WAFv2 (managed Core Rule Set + Known Bad Inputs + per-IP rate limit) sits in front of the public webhook via CloudFront, with logging/metrics enabled.
IAM remains well-scoped across all roles, reinforced by the new cloudtrail_to_cw role following the same minimal-scope pattern.

findings.title: Detective controls substantially implemented (CloudTrail + GuardDuty + IAM/Secrets alarms), but notification path unwired and Config/Security Hub still absent
findings.impact: CloudTrail provides a real, tamper-evident audit trail and GuardDuty provides automatic anomaly detection, but neither the two new CloudWatch alarms nor any GuardDuty finding is routed to a human/on-call system by default (no aws_sns_topic anywhere in the repo). The CloudTrail bucket policy also lacks an aws:SourceArn condition (narrow confused-deputy risk).
findings.recommendation: Create an SNS topic and populate var.alarm_actions to close the notification loop for all 5 module alarms; add aws:SourceArn conditions to the CloudTrail bucket policy; consider AWS Config/Security Hub once past POC scale.

alternative.summary: Wire an SNS topic + subscription now vs. leave console-only
pros: Closes the actionability gap for both new and pre-existing alarms in one change
Also resolves part of Operational Excellence's OPS-F2 as a side effect
cons: Needs a real destination decided outside Terraform

findings.title: WAF/CloudFront front in place, but the raw API Gateway origin remains directly reachable (residual bypass, unchanged)
findings.impact: Traffic sent directly to the execute-api URL skips WAF managed rules and the rate rule, though still bound by API Gateway throttle and HMAC check. No unauthenticated write path exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared-secret custom header set only by CloudFront's origin custom headers, checked in the Lambda before HMAC verification.

alternative.summary: CloudFront custom-header origin-verification vs. accept as residual risk
pros: Closes the bypass at negligible cost/complexity
cons: One more secret to rotate and keep in sync

findings.title: No customer-managed KMS keys (CMK); blocked at the account level (unchanged)
findings.impact: Every data store, including the new CloudTrail bucket, uses AWS-managed/owned keys.
findings.recommendation: Request narrow kms:CreateKey/key-management permissions, then re-enable kms_key_id across all data stores and enable automatic rotation.

cons: Blocked by an org-level IAM deny

findings.title: Bedrock model-invoke permission scoped wider than the models actually used (unchanged)
findings.impact: Runtime role can invoke any foundation model in any region.
findings.recommendation: Scope the BedrockInvoke Resource to the two configured model ARNs/region.

findings.title: Unpinned Python dependencies, no lockfile (unchanged)
findings.impact: Builds not reproducible; may silently pick up vulnerable dependency versions.
findings.recommendation: Pin exact versions or use a lockfile; add pip-audit/Dependabot.

improvements.text: Create an SNS topic and populate var.alarm_actions so all 5 CloudWatch alarms actually notify someone (SEC-F3)
Add aws:SourceArn condition to the CloudTrail S3 bucket policy statements (SEC-F3)
Add a CloudFront origin custom-header check in the webhook Lambda (SEC-F1)
Scope Bedrock InvokeModel resource to configured model ARNs (SEC-F4)
Pin Python dependency versions and add vulnerability scanning (SEC-F5)
Evaluate AWS Config and/or Security Hub once past POC scale (SEC-F3)
Reintroduce customer-managed KMS keys once unblocked (SEC-F2)

pillars.notes: Static analysis only (live_aws=OFF). Evaluated the current working tree including uncommitted observability/cloudtrail.tf (new) and variables.tf (modified). SEC-F3's severity moved Medium->Low (real risk reduction) but the SEC-10 criterion verdict stayed Partial->Partial because Config/Security Hub remain absent and neither new alarms nor GuardDuty findings have a default notification path — this is why the pillar score (81/100) did not move even though real, correctly-built security work was verified. SEC-F1/F2/F4/F5 re-verified fresh, unchanged. No Critical findings; no capping.

roadmap.action: Create an SNS topic and populate var.alarm_actions so all 5 CloudWatch alarms actually notify someone
Add aws:SourceArn condition to the CloudTrail S3 bucket policy statements
Add a CloudFront origin custom-header check in the webhook Lambda to reject direct API Gateway traffic
Scope the Bedrock InvokeModel resource to the two configured model ARNs and region
Pin Python dependencies with a lock file; enable Dependabot/pip-audit
Evaluate AWS Config and/or Security Hub once past POC scale
Reintroduce customer-managed KMS keys once the account-level kms:CreateKey deny is lifted
